newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal copper miners back temporary deal.
newsitem.headline: Portugal copper miners back temporary deal.

text.p: Miners at the Neves Corvo copper mine in southern Portugal approved a temporary deal negotiated by union leaders to return to work on Monday after a week-long strike.
Under the deal, management is due to present a new proposal for the operation of continuous working at the 107,000 tonnes per year mine by Wednesday.
But union leader Eduardo Lazaro told Reuters that even if the proposal was not ready by mid-week, there were no plans for a return to the stoppage which had paralysed production.
Miners had protested against company plans for Sunday shifts which management says are vital to the competitivity of the mine, 250 km south of Lisbon.

Under the temporary accord, negotiatied by union leaders, management and representatives of the government in the early hours of Saturday, the company plan will include Sunday working along with more holidays and other benefits for miners.
